# How to Create Social Media Graphics with Midjourney in 10 Minutes

> **In short:** Midjourney turns your text descriptions into original images in under a minute, which makes it perfect for Instagram and Facebook posts. You'll need a paid subscription (no free plan) and a web browser. One honest limit: it can't reliably render text inside images, so plan to add your captions in a separate tool.

You don't need Photoshop, Canva Pro, or a graphic design background to make eye-catching posts anymore. Midjourney is an AI image generator — think of it as a digital artist who paints whatever you describe in plain English. Give it one sentence and it gives you back four image options in under a minute. From a cozy coffee shop announcement to a product launch hero shot, you describe it and Midjourney draws it.

## Before you start
- A Midjourney account with an active paid subscription (the Basic plan starts at around $10/month; there is no free option).
- A modern web browser on a computer or phone (Chrome, Safari, Edge, Firefox all work).
- A rough idea of your post — subject, mood, colors, and which platform you're posting to.
- About 10 minutes total.

## Step 1 — Sign in and open the create page
Go to **midjourney.com** in your browser and click **Sign In** in the top-right corner. Log in with the same account you used to subscribe — Google, Discord, or email all work. Once you're in, look for a button labeled **Create** or **Imagine**, usually in the left sidebar or as a large button at the top of your dashboard. Click it and the image generator opens, with a big text box in the middle of the screen ready for your idea. If you don't see a Create button, look for a **+** icon or a section labeled **Generate** instead — Midjourney updates its layout often, but the prompt box is always near the center of the screen.
💬 Example: click into the empty box and type your idea (we'll write the actual prompt in the next step).
You'll know it worked when you see a large empty text box labeled something like "Imagine" or "Describe what you want to create."

## Step 2 — Describe your graphic in one clear sentence
Click into the prompt box and write a short, concrete description of the image you want. The more specific you are, the closer the result will match what you imagined. Start with the subject ("a small bakery storefront at sunrise"), then add the mood or style ("warm golden light, watercolor style, cozy"), and end with the aspect ratio for your platform. For Instagram square posts, add **--ar 1:1** at the end. For Instagram portrait or Facebook feed, use **--ar 4:5**. For Stories or Reels, use **--ar 9:16**. Press Enter or click the **Generate** button and wait about a minute.
💬 Example: `a small artisan bakery storefront at sunrise, warm golden light, watercolor illustration style, soft pastel colors --ar 1:1`
You'll know it worked when four image previews appear on your screen within about 60 seconds.

## Step 3 — Pick your favorite (or ask for variations)
Once the four images appear, you'll see a row of small buttons labeled **U1, U2, U3, U4** underneath them. These mean "Upscale" and turn that specific image into a high-resolution version. You'll also see **V1, V2, V3, V4** — these mean "Variation" and ask Midjourney to make four new versions of that image, keeping the same idea but tweaking it slightly. Click a **V** button if you like the composition but want a different style. If one of the four images is already perfect, click its **U** button to make it bigger and sharper. The V buttons give you control, the U buttons commit to a choice.
💬 Example: click **U2** to upscale the second image, or click **V3** to get four new takes on the third.
You'll know it worked when one image grows larger and crisper (Upscale) or four new variations appear (Variation).

## Step 4 — Download the full-size image
After clicking an Upscale button, the enlarged version appears on your screen. Look for a **download icon** — usually a small arrow pointing down into a tray, or three dots ⋯ that open a menu with "Download" inside. Click it and the image saves to your Downloads folder as a PNG file. If you can't find a download button, right-click (or long-press on a phone) the image itself and choose **Save image as** — that's a reliable backup method that works on every browser and never breaks when the interface changes.
💬 Example: name the file something you'll recognize later, like `bakery-post-instagram.png`, before saving.
You'll know it worked when you can open the file on your computer or phone and it looks crisp at the size you need for posting.

## Step 5 — Add text and your logo in a free tool
This is the honest part: Midjourney is excellent at pictures but unreliable at rendering readable text inside images — letters often come out garbled or misspelled. So once you've downloaded your image, open it in a free tool like **Canva** (the free tier is enough), **Google Slides**, or even your phone's built-in photo editor. Add your caption, logo, price tag, or call-to-action as a text overlay on top of the AI-generated background. This two-step process gives you the best of both worlds: a beautiful custom image plus perfectly readable text.
💬 Example: in Canva, click "Upload" to add your Midjourney image, then click "Text" on the left and add "Fresh croissants daily!" in your brand font.
You'll know it worked when your final image looks polished, the text is crisp, and it feels ready to post.

## Step 6 — Post it to Instagram or Facebook
Open Instagram or Facebook on your phone or computer, create a new post, and upload your finished image. Add your caption, hashtags, and tag any relevant accounts. If you're on a paid Midjourney plan, you generally own what you generate and can use it commercially — but double-check Midjourney's current terms of service, since some platforms are starting to require labels for AI-made images.
💬 Example: caption — "Saturday morning, fresh from the oven ☕ #smallbusiness #bakery"
You'll know it worked when your post is live and people start reacting.

## Common mistakes
- **Writing vague prompts like "make something pretty."** Midjourney needs specifics — subject, mood, color, style. The fix: spend 10 extra seconds adding details like "soft pastel colors, watercolor style, morning light."
- **Forgetting to set the aspect ratio.** A square 1:1 prompt makes a square; if you post a landscape image to Instagram, it'll get cropped awkwardly. The fix: always add `--ar 1:1`, `--ar 4:5`, or `--ar 9:16` to match where you're posting.
- **Asking Midjourney to write text inside the image.** Letters almost always come out wrong. The fix: generate the background in Midjourney, then add your caption in Canva or any free editor (covered in Step 5).
- **Expecting a free tier that no longer exists.** Midjourney stopped offering free generations back in 2023. The fix: budget for the Basic plan (around $10/month) or look at free alternatives like Microsoft Designer's image creator if cost is a concern.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** Need a custom birthday card, a unique profile picture, or a one-off invitation? Midjourney makes it in under a minute — no design skills required.
- **For your business or work:** Save hundreds of dollars on stock photos and freelance designers. Every social media post can have a custom, on-brand image instead of the same generic stock photos your competitors are using.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with one image you'll actually post this week. Don't get stuck browsing hundreds of generations — pick a winner, add your text, and ship it.

## Try it now
Open midjourney.com, sign in, and type this prompt into the create box: `a steaming cup of coffee on a wooden table next to an open book, soft morning light, cozy lifestyle photo style --ar 4:5`. Generate it, upscale your favorite, and save it. That's your first AI-made social media graphic — done in under three minutes.
